name: Tile Matching Solitaire
description: Solitaire game using around 144 tiles (traditionally Mah Jong). Tiles are stacked in layers with horizontal rows; each row rests on the row below. Remove all tiles by taking matching pairs of exposed tiles (a tile is exposed when at the end of a row and not covered).

overview.description: Solitaire game using around 144 tiles (traditionally Mah Jong). Tiles are stacked in layers with horizontal rows; each row rests on the row below. Remove all tiles by taking matching pairs of exposed tiles (a tile is exposed when at the end of a row and not covered).

history.origins: Tile matching solitaire originated as a computer game and exists in many versions (e.g. Shanghai, Taipei, Kyodai), using Mah Jong or similar tiles in matching sets of four.
timeline: 1980s: Originated as a computer game; Shanghai and similar titles released.
history.cultural: Popular as casual and online solitaire; often bundled with operating systems or played in browsers.
history.evolution: Originated as a computer game; many versions (Shanghai, Taipei, Kyodai, Moraff's) with various tile designs and layouts.

setup.players: Single player. This solitaire is played by one person, who clears the layout by removing matching pairs of exposed tiles (tiles at the end of a row and not covered).
setup.deck: Set of around 144 tiles (Mah Jong traditionally).
setup.dealing: Tiles are stacked in layers; each layer has horizontal rows. Tiles in a row rest on the row below. Remove pairs of exposed (uncovered) matching tiles until the layout is clear.

rules.objective: Remove all tiles from the layout by taking matching pairs of exposed tiles.
rules.gameplay: A tile is available when it is at the end of a row and not covered. Remove two matching tiles at a time. Layout is built in layers; clear the tableau to win.
keyRules: Only exposed tiles (end of row, nothing on top) can be played.
Remove tiles in matching pairs only.
Some deals may be unsolvable; many computer versions guarantee a solution.

strategy.basic: Prefer removing pairs that free the most tiles; avoid blocking tiles needed for later matches.
strategy.intermediate: Track which tile types still have covered copies; delay removing a pair if it blocks access to others.
strategy.advanced: Full lookahead to ensure the layout remains solvable; some orders of removal lead to dead ends.
tips: Expose tiles from lower layers first when possible.
Computer versions often guarantee solvable layouts; physical random deals may be unwinnable.

variations.name: Mahjong Connect
variations.description: Pairs of tiles can only be removed if they can be connected by a clear orthogonal path, often with not more than a given number of right-angle bends.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant differs in removal rule only; no engine constant overrides documented in source.

scoring.description: No point scoring; win by clearing the layout.
scoring.winCondition: Remove all tiles from the layout by matching and removing exposed pairs.

synthesis.shortDescription: Solitaire game using domino or mahjong-style tile matching.
